IS 13785:1993 4 PACKING
For retail packing up to 1 kg, LDPE bags of 007 mm minimum thickness shall be used, their mouth heat seaied. For packs up to 500 g cartons ( see IS 6604 : 1991 ) shall be used. However, cartons for packs of 1 kg capacity shall be made of `E' fluted corrugated board consisting of 240 gsm duplex board/80 gsm kraft paper/80 gsm kraft paper. In addition, the requirements as given in IS 8190 ( Part 1 ) : 1988 shall be followed. 5 MARKING The containers shall be securely closed and shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information and any other information as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed thereunder: a) b) c) d) e) f) g) h) Name of the material; Name of the manufacturer; Date of manufacture; Batch number; Date of expiry; Net mass of the contents; Dodine content, percent ( m/m ); and A cautionary notice worded as in the Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules. drawn according to IS 10627 : 1983 and tested within 90 days of its manufacture. When the material is offered for inspection after 90 days sampling shall be done of its manufacture, according to IS 10627 : 1983. However, the criteria for conformity of the material when tested, shall be the limits of tolerances, as applicable over the declared nominal value and given under 3.4 of this standard. 7 TESTS 7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate methods referred to in 3.3,3.4 and co1 4 of Table 1. 7.2 Suspeusibility For suspensibility test, start with O-5 percent of concentration and carry out the test as described in 11.2 of IS 6940 : 1982. Transfer the bottom 25 ml portion of suspension and sediment into a reaction flask. Wash the cylinder thrice, each time with 100 ml of methanoI and quantitatively transfer to the reaction flask. Evaporate to dryness. Proceed to determined dodine content as described in Annex A of IS 13784 : 1993. 7.3 Quality of Reagents Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS 1070 : 1992 ) shall be employed in tests. NOTE`Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

6 SAMPLING When freshly manufactured material is offered for inspection, representative samples shall be

ANNEX A J Clause -3.3, Table 1, Item (i) ]
DETERMINATION A-l PRINCIPLE Dodine is extracted using isopropanol which is distilled off and the residue obtained is dissolved in acetic acid and acetic anhydride and titrated against perchloric acid using crystal violet as indicator. A-2 APPARATUS A-2.B Vacuum Pump A-2.2 G-4 Crucible A-3 REAGENTS A-3.1 Isopropanol 2 OF DODINE CONTENT A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Weigh accurately about 1 g of the sample and transfer quantitatively into a 250-ml separating funnel. Add 50 ml isopropanol. Extract for 10 minutes and filter through G-4 crucible. Wash the separating funnel as well as the crucible thrice, each time 25 ml of isopropanol. Transfer the contents to a 250-ml Erlenmeyer flask. Evaporate isopropanol on water bath to complete dryness. Take the residue and proceed to determine the dodine content by the method prescribed in Annex A of IS 13784 : 1993.

1 Standard

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by Details of conditions under BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to ~promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attenting to connected matters in the country. Copyright No part of these publications may be reproduced BIS has copyright of all its publications. in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Revision of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and <Standards Monthly Additions'.
